```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
options(width = 72)
```

Observations belong to things: a subject, a session, a run, a stimulus.
Describing those things once, in their own tables, keeps covariates such as a
subject's age or a stimulus's category in one place instead of copied onto
every row. This vignette shows how a frame refers to such *entities*, how a
*study* links several frames that share them, and how a *collection* holds
frames that cannot share a feature space. It assumes the basics from
`vignette("fmridataset")`.

```{r}
library(fmridataset)
set.seed(5)
```

## Entities and relations

An entity is a table with one row per thing and a key column that identifies
it. Here there are two subjects and four stimuli.

```{r entities}
subjects <- entity_frame(
  data.frame(
    subject_id = c("sub-01", "sub-02"),
    group = c("patient", "control"),
    age = c(34, 29)
  ),
  key = "subject_id",
  entity_type = "subject"
)
stimuli <- entity_frame(
  data.frame(
    stimulus_id = c("face-1", "face-2", "house-1", "house-2"),
    category = c("face", "face", "house", "house")
  ),
  key = "stimulus_id",
  entity_type = "stimulus"
)
subjects
```

A frame refers to entities through *relations*: a `key_relation()` says that
a column of the observation table holds keys of an entity. The frame below
holds one beta estimate per trial for three regions, and each trial names its
subject and its stimulus.

```{r betas}
regions <- index_space(3, ids = c("FFA", "PPA", "V1"))
trials <- data.frame(
  .obs_id = sprintf("%s-trial-%d", rep(c("sub-01", "sub-02"), each = 4), 1:4),
  subject_id = rep(c("sub-01", "sub-02"), each = 4),
  stimulus_id = rep(c("face-1", "house-1", "face-2", "house-2"), 2),
  onset = rep(c(0, 8, 16, 24), 2)
)

betas <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(beta = matrix(round(rnorm(8 * 3), 2), 8, 3)),
  observations = trials,
  space = regions,
  entities = list(subject = subjects, stimulus = stimuli),
  relations = list(
    trial_subject = key_relation("subject_id", target = "subject"),
    trial_stimulus = key_relation("stimulus_id", target = "stimulus")
  )
)
```

Construction checks every key: a trial that named a subject missing from the
subject table would be an error. With `resolve = TRUE`, the observation table
gains each entity's columns, prefixed with the entity name.

```{r resolve}
resolved <- observations(betas, resolve = TRUE)
resolved[, c(".obs_id", "subject.group", "stimulus.category")]
```

Filters can use those columns directly.

```{r filter-entity}
faces <- filter_observations(betas, stimulus.category == "face")
observation_ids(faces)
```

Entities can also point at each other, for example runs at subjects with
`key_relation("subject_id", source = "run", target = "subject")`, and an
observation then reaches its subject through its run. `read_bids_bold()`
builds exactly this structure for every import.

## Studies: several frames, shared entities

An analysis rarely has one frame. The same subjects have a BOLD time series
and the trial-wise betas estimated from it. An `fmri_study()` holds both,
with one authoritative copy of the entities they share.

```{r bold}
volumes <- data.frame(
  .obs_id = sprintf("%s-vol-%02d", rep(c("sub-01", "sub-02"), each = 16), 1:16),
  subject_id = rep(c("sub-01", "sub-02"), each = 16),
  run_id = rep(c("sub-01-run-1", "sub-02-run-1"), each = 16),
  TR = 2
)
bold <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(bold = matrix(round(rnorm(32 * 3), 2), 32, 3)),
  observations = volumes,
  space = regions,
  entities = list(subject = subjects),
  relations = list(
    volume_subject = key_relation("subject_id", target = "subject")
  )
)
```

A *link* records how the rows of one frame correspond to the rows of another.
Here each trial maps to the volume acquired at its onset.

```{r link}
onset_volume <- frame_link(
  "betas", "bold",
  type = "correspondence",
  map = data.frame(
    .source_id = trials$.obs_id,
    .target_id = sprintf("%s-vol-%02d", trials$subject_id, trials$onset / 2 + 1)
  )
)
onset_volume

study <- fmri_study(
  list(bold = bold, betas = betas),
  entities = list(subject = subjects, stimulus = stimuli),
  links = list(trial_onset = onset_volume)
)
study
```

The study checks that every frame's entities agree with its shared copy and
that every link names IDs that exist. `filter_entities()` then selects
entities once and applies the selection everywhere: every frame keeps only
the rows of the selected subjects, and the link keeps only their pairs.

```{r filter-study}
patients <- filter_entities(study, subject, group == "patient")
n_observations(study_frame(patients, "bold"))
n_observations(study_frame(patients, "betas"))
study_link(patients, "trial_onset")$map
```

Nothing is read: the filtered frames are views over the original arrays.

## Collections: same design, different spaces

Data in each subject's native space cannot share a feature axis, because one
subject's voxels are not another's. `bind_observations()` refuses to stack
them.

```{r native}
native <- lapply(c("sub-01", "sub-02"), function(subject) {
  fmri_frame(
    assays = list(bold = matrix(rnorm(4 * 18), 4, 18)),
    observations = data.frame(
      .obs_id = sprintf("%s-vol-%d", subject, 1:4),
      run_id = "run-1",
      TR = 2
    ),
    space = volume_space(c(3, 3, 2), template = paste0(subject, "-native"))
  )
})
names(native) <- c("sub-01", "sub-02")
```

```{r native-bind, error = TRUE}
bind_observations(native[["sub-01"]], native[["sub-02"]])
```

An `fmri_collection()` holds such frames side by side instead. It requires
them to share the same observation columns and assays, and it keeps each
frame's own space.

```{r collection}
cohort <- fmri_collection(native)
cohort
same_space(
  space(collection_frame(cohort, "sub-01")),
  space(collection_frame(cohort, "sub-02"))
)
```

A collection can be one representation of a study, alongside frames in a
common space, so a study can hold native-space time series and
template-space betas for the same subjects.

To save any of these to disk, see `vignette("persistence-and-import")`.
